title: Long TBT — April Payrolls +115K Shock + June FOMC Hike Live (Reload)
entry: Initiate $34.80-36.50 (30Y at 4.95-5.05%). Scale: 60% at current; add 40% on a confirmed daily close above 5.05% on the 30Y (TBT approximately $36.50-37.00) or on a hot May NFP print (June 5). This is a reload of the prior TBT position (all targets hit at $37.63), entered at a lower cost basis ($35.66 vs. prior $28.50) with appropriately higher targets.
stop_loss: $33.50 daily close (30Y below ~4.75%) — implies Warsh adopts an explicitly dovish stance at June 17 FOMC, OR May NFP prints below 50K forcing a full pivot narrative, OR a broad flight-to-safety bond rally drives 30Y sustainably lower
targets: $37.50 — 30Y back above 5.10%; May NFP (June 5) runs hot for the second consecutive month; Warsh pre-FOMC communication reaffirms the 8-4 hawkish baseline; +5.2%
$39.50 — 30Y at 5.20-5.25%; Warsh's June 17 FOMC signals a rate hike at the July meeting; market prices >80% probability of a 2026 hike; +10.8%
$43.00 — 30Y at 5.35%+; Warsh delivers a June 17 hike OR signals July delivery with explicit inflation data justification; bear steepening regime; +20.6%
catalyst: April payrolls printed at +115,000 — nearly double the 62-65K consensus — with unemployment holding at 4.3%. The labor market is running significantly hotter than the Fed's models assume in their 'soft landing' scenario. May NFP (Friday June 5) has a high base-rate probability of printing similarly hot given the structural employment demand from AI capex buildout, defense spending expansion, and infrastructure investment. The June 17 Warsh FOMC inherits: (1) an 8-4 hawkish voting split from the April meeting, (2) April PCE at approximately 3.3% core, (3) two consecutive above-consensus payroll prints, and (4) Brent at $93.37 adding energy-driven inflation re-acceleration risk. The 30Y at 4.99% is pinned at the Day-2 confirmation level from the prior framework — one more hot data point resets it above 5.05% and opens the TBT trade.
thesis:
TBT (ProShares UltraShort 20+ Year Treasury, 2x inverse) is the cleanest expression of the hawkish-rates thesis that the prior TBT position already validated (all three targets hit, closed at $37.63). The reload is justified by new information not available when the original position was created: April payrolls at +115K is the single most important new data point. The Fed's implicit dual mandate model requires both a cool inflation reading AND a softening labor market to justify a pause or cut. The April payrolls figure (+115K, nearly double the consensus) removes the 'cooling labor market' leg from any dovish argument Warsh might want to make. The hot labor market competes directly with AI-capex-driven productivity narratives: it means the economy is not the soft-landing-at-stall-speed story that would allow the Fed to stay on hold indefinitely.

The mechanics of TBT's leverage make the reload entry more favorable than it appears. The prior TBT was entered at $28.50 and closed at $37.63 — a $9.13 move (+32%) from a starting 30Y of approximately 5.05%. The reload enters at $35.66 with 30Y at 4.99%. The path from 4.99% to 5.20% (Target 2 level) is a 21-basis-point move — smaller than the 2024 move of approximately 45bps that drove the prior TBT from $28.50 to $37.63. TBT's 2x leverage on the 20+ year Treasury means every 10bps rise in the 30Y generates approximately 2.5-3.5% TBT price appreciation (the duration of long TLT is approximately 17 years, so 10bps × 17 × 2 = 3.4% TBT move). From 4.99% to 5.20% = 21bps × 3.4% per 10bps ≈ 7.1% TBT appreciation, which maps to $35.66 × 1.071 = $38.19 — consistent with Target 1 at $37.50 and Target 2 at $39.50.

The three-week window is tight but defined by two binary catalysts: May NFP on June 5 and Warsh's June 17 FOMC. If both print hot/hawkish, TBT reaches Target 2 ($39.50) within the window. If only one delivers (NFP hot but Warsh cautious), Target 1 ($37.50) is the likely resting point. The stop at $33.50 requires a 30Y decline to approximately 4.75%, which necessitates either a genuine Fed pivot signal or a significant risk-off bond rally — both of which are low-probability given the April payrolls data.

The portfolio construction rationale: TBT is the only direct rates hedge in the active book. UUP (active) provides a dollar safe-haven overlay, but UUP gains depend on the interest-rate differential channel, while TBT gains come from the direct yield-curve move. They are complementary, not redundant. The combined 5% allocation (TBT 3% + UUP 2%) provides meaningful portfolio protection if both the June 5 NFP and June 17 FOMC print hawkish signals simultaneously — the highest-risk macro event in the next 3 weeks for the predominantly long-equity book.
bull_case: May NFP (June 5) prints +100K+ for the second consecutive month; Warsh's pre-FOMC communication (likely June 10-12 window) signals the FOMC is 'actively discussing' a June hike; 30Y closes above 5.10% before June 17. TBT reaches $37.50 (Target 1) by June 10. June 17 FOMC: Warsh hikes 25bps and signals another one is possible in July if inflation doesn't cool. 30Y to 5.25%; TBT to $39.50 (Target 2). Tail: June 5 NFP prints above +150K — a third consecutive above-consensus print — drives 30Y immediately to 5.15-5.20%, TBT gaps to $38-39 in a single session.
bear_case: May NFP disappoints at +30-50K, signaling the April print was a statistical outlier; 30Y falls from 4.99% toward 4.80% on the soft print. Warsh adopts a 'patient and data-dependent' tone at June 17 — the 8-4 hawkish vote doesn't translate into explicit forward guidance. TBT falls to $33.50-34.00 range; stop triggered. Tail: Iran signs the MoU deal before June 5, Brent collapses to $85-88, energy-driven inflation rolls over, and the PCE trajectory for May is expected to be clean — the entire hawkish rates narrative de-escalates simultaneously, driving 30Y to 4.70% and TBT to $31.
invalidation: $33.50 daily close (30Y sustainably below 4.75%), OR May NFP (June 5) prints below 50K and Warsh explicitly takes a June hike off the table in post-meeting communications, OR Warsh June 17 press conference is clearly dovish with no explicit hike guidance

outcome.outcome_label: Target 3 hit at $43.00 — 30Y yield regime shift confirmed
outcome.note: TBT surged through all three targets as the Warsh FOMC (June 16-17) approaches with an 8-4 hawkish baseline and 20% rate-hike tail odds. Goldman Sachs called no 2026 cuts (first cut June 2027), and May NFP ran hot. 30Y held elevated above 4.90%, driving TBT from the $35.77 reference price to $44-46 — a 20.2% gain to T3 ($43). TBT continues running above T3 on June 16 as FOMC opens. Formally closed at T3 per system rules; re-entry position initiated at the T3 breakout (see long-tbt-warsh-fomc-hawkish-reentry-2026-06-16).
